subject.title: fix(line): cap message action text length

question: For LINE message actions exceeding the vendor’s 300-grapheme limit, should OpenClaw normalize the tapped text to its first 300 graphemes rather than reject the entire action payload?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically aligned with LINE’s counting contract, but truncation intentionally changes the exact text sent when a user taps an over-limit command-like action; source and tests cannot establish the preferred user-facing overflow policy.

options.title: Approve centralized truncation
options.body: Accept the proposed shared 300-grapheme cap so invalid LINE actions become deliverable while valid emoji and combining graphemes remain intact.

options.title: Require explicit overflow handling
options.body: Pause this PR and design a channel-visible error or mapped-command/postback strategy for cases where a truncated tapped text could change meaning.

recommendation.title: Approve centralized truncation
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed shared 300-grapheme cap so invalid LINE actions become deliverable while valid emoji and combining graphemes remain intact.
